newsitem.title: USA: Prudential sees modest aluminum surplus in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Prudential sees modest aluminum surplus in 1997.

text.p: The aluminum market will end 1997 with a modest 61,200 tonne surplus, switching to a large 463,900 tonne deficit in 1998, broker Prudential Securities said in a report.
Prudential forecast an average ingot price up 7.5 percent in 1997 to 72 cents per pound, and rising 15.3 percent in 1998 to 83 cents. LME cash settled at 69 cents on Tuesday.

"The world aluminum industry appears to have bottomed out, but it cannot be said it has turned the corner, the latter of which may not occur until at least the second quarter of 1997," Prudential said.
Prudential said it recently raised its rating on shares of Alumax from hold to buy, and placed a strong hold rating on four other producers, Alcoa, Alcan, Reynolds Metals, and Kaiser Aluminum.
"We will watch closely for any acceleration in the turnaround which is being partially discounted in the share price of the last four companies," Prudential said.
Several other analysts expected the market to move into a deficit next year.
